title: l-5-Methyltetrahydrofolate supplementation increases blood folate concentrations to a greater extent than folic acid supplementation in Malaysian women
authors: Henderson AM, Aleliunas RE, Loh SP, Khor GL, Harvey-Leeson S, Glier MB, et al.
population: Healthy women aged 20 to 45 years in Malaysia, without mandatory fortification
funder: Supported by funding from the Advanced Foods and Materials Network Centre of Excellence of Canada and the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC); investigator grant from BC Children's Hospital Research Institute; NSERC and University of British Columbia student awards.
result: Results read from the published abstract. Folic acid 1 mg, an equimolar 1.13 mg L-5-methyl-THF, or placebo daily. At 12 weeks red cell folate was 1951 ± 496 nmol/L with L-5-methyl-THF, 1498 ± 580 with folic acid (P = 0.003 between them) and 958 ± 345 with placebo; plasma folate medians 52.0, 40.1 and 12.6 nmol/L. Homocysteine was 15% and 17% lower than placebo in the two active groups, without difference between them; vitamin B12, other methyl metabolites and monocyte LINE-1 methylation did not differ.
